invention_name: Combination Hammer and Lumber Manipulating Tool
disclaimer: Please note this is a hypothetical technology presented solely for demonstration purposes. This report is a sample/demo deliverable of the inventionevaluator platform; content is derived from a retrospective evaluation of an expired patent conducted from public records.

technology.basis: Derived from report findings P-03-001/P-03-002 (fixed-geometry single-tool integration, no moving parts, two mounting configurations), P-04-001 (crowded B25D class, few direct equivalents), P-03-004a (LOW regulatory hurdle), P-03-003/P-03-005 (concept stage, no performance or prototype data established).

ip.basis: Derived from report findings P-02-006 (US term expired 2017-06-13; CA expired 2018-06-12 — no enforceable exclusivity), P-05-007 (NOT ANTICIPATED by identified references), P-04-001 (crowded class). IP asset is granted but lapsed: exclusivity value is nil.

market.basis: Derived from report findings P-07-002 (US hand tools USD 6.1B 2024, CAGR 3.4%; hammer CAGR 3.0-4.5%), P-07-004 (premium tier 45-55% of revenue; high competitive intensity), P-02-006 (expired — free-to-practice concept only), P-07-001 (no commercial adoption established).

commercialization_summary.paragraph: Commercial actionability is Moderate (market size medium-high, mature low-growth category, high competitive intensity). The US patent expired June 13, 2017 and the Canadian family member expired June 12, 2018: the fixed-jaw hammer concept is now in the public domain, so commercial value exists only as a free-to-practice product concept — there is no IP left to license. Commercial adoption could not be established from the completed evidence protocol.
teasers: No exclusivity remains: US term expired 2017-06-13; CA term expired 2018-06-12.
Estwing and Vaughan & Bushnell identified as the strongest fit pathways for a framing-focused fixed-jaw hammer.

tech_ladder.basis: The invention is a single integrated tool (hammer-head + fixed jaw on one device); no system-level integration is claimed.

dev_ladder.basis: P-03-003/P-03-005/P-03-006: no prototype, test, or production evidence established.
